name: Replication Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday replication work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical replication tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday replication work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical replication tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Before starting replication work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
2. Keep replication outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
3. State assumptions about replication explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
4. Surface known limitations of a chosen replication approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
5. Prefer explicit, readable replication solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
6. Validate replication outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
7. Measure before optimizing any replication bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
8. Check that replication terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated replication concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of replication correctness.
- Do not apply generic replication advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid introducing new replication abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not silently drop replication edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for replication, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
